rv.q: Thanks to a fizzier and more fluent second half this is a musical that leaves one feeling well entertained.
It all makes for a perfectly pleasant show in which only the songs, in adding depth to character, put a brake on the story's propulsion.
"Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown" may have a clunky title – that is a nightmare to keep typing – but is a fantastic show from start to finish.

… It's super-smart songwriting: all discord and layers to make your head swim. Structurally, Lane's book carries the same delirium, deploying the absurdist rhythms of a demented Dario Fo farce, but it suffers – badly – from naffness… Even Greig, who can't help but be likeable, has to mime Pepa's emotional rollercoaster with spluttered...
